jobs.title: JPL Deputy Director
jobs.description:
Job Details

New ideas are all around us, but only a few will change the world. That’s our focus at JPL. We ask the biggest questions, then search the universe for answers—literally. We build upon ideas that have guided generations, then share our discoveries to inspire generations to come. Your mission—your opportunity—is to seek out the answers that bring us one step closer. If you’re driven to discover, create, and inspire something that lasts a lifetime and beyond, you’re ready for JPL.

Located in Pasadena, California, JPL has a campus-like environment situated on 177 acres in the foothills of the San Gabriel Mountains and offers a work environment unlike any other: we inspire passion, foster innovation, build collaboration, and reward excellence.

Summary

The Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), a federally funded research and development center managed by the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) for NASA, is seeking an exceptional executive leader to serve as its Deputy Director/Chief Operating Officer and help shape the future of one of the world's premier aerospace and research institutions, enabling groundbreaking discoveries, advancing national priorities, and supporting missions that expand humanity's understanding of Earth, the solar system, and the universe. Partnering closely with the Director, the Deputy Director will provide strategic leadership, institutional stewardship, and operational excellence across a complex enterprise of scientific, engineering, and administrative functions. The successful candidate will empower a world-class workforce while strengthening the partnerships, capabilities, and organizational resilience necessary to achieve JPL's ambitious mission now and into the future.

Job Summary

The Deputy Director of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory is appointed by the Vice President/ Director of JPL with the concurrence of the President of the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), which manages JPL for NASA, and in consultation with the NASA Administrator.

Reporting to the JPL Director, the Deputy Director serves as the Laboratory's Chief Operating Officer, providing executive leadership for institutional operations and mission execution. The Deputy Director leads and integrates the Executive Council, drives organizational execution and accountability, and provides strategic leadership for the Laboratory's workforce. As a strategic partner to the Director, the Deputy Director orchestrates cross-functional coordination among Business, Operations, and Programmatic leadership while maintaining institutional alignment and operational continuity. The Deputy Director ensures operational excellence, fosters a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement, and engages in strategic relationships with NASA, Caltech, the Department of War, Intelligence Community, and Space Force. Through integrated execution across programmatic and institutional functions, the Deputy Director ensures operational excellence across all Laboratory functions, driving continuous improvement while deepening the critical Caltech-JPL partnership.

Key Responsibilities

Executive Leadership

Provide executive leadership and ensure integration of the Laboratory's institutional operations, which includes acquisitions, workforce management, infrastructure, facilities, and administrative organizations.
Partner with the JPL Director to establish institutional priorities, execute strategic initiatives, and advance the Laboratory's long-term vision.
Continue to strengthen and advance the close and enduring partnership with Caltech
Serve as Acting Director, when delegated, exercising full authority for Laboratory operations and executive decision-making.
Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, integrity, and continuous improvement.
Support and partner with the Director in leading the Laboratory through periods of organizational change while maintaining workforce engagement, operational continuity, and mission success.
Chair the weekly Executive Council, facilitating Laboratory-wide decision-making, policy development, and organizational alignment.

Strategic Institutional Leadership

Assume a leadership role in the development and execution of JPL's long-range institutional strategy, which includes aligning workforce, infrastructure, technology investments, and operational capabilities with future mission needs. Ensure Executive Council alignment on institutional strategy and drive integrated execution across programmatic and institutional functions.
Initiate organizational assessments and continuous improvement initiatives to enhance institutional effectiveness.
Oversee Laboratory-level governance, management systems, and enterprise decision making processes to ensure transparency, accountability, compliance, and organizational performance.
Deepen the enduring partnership with Caltech administration, participating in Caltech Board of Trustees engagements concerning JPL.

Programmatic Oversight

Chair Center Project Management Reviews (PMR) to evaluate mission readiness, risk posture, and programmatic execution across all spaceflight and scientific projects.
Serve as JPL's senior representative to the NASA Office of JPL Management and Oversight (NOJMO), while acting as the primary institutional liaison with NASA and Caltech functional leadership.
Ensure effective integration of mission, compliance, and institutional functions across the organization.
With the Director, lead JPL's strategic relationships with the Department of War, the Intelligence Community, and the U.S. Space Force, serving as the primary executive interface for national security programs.

Institutional Processes and Operations

Facilitate cross-functional coordination among Business, Operations, and Programmatic leadership to drive aligned execution and resolve cross-functional institutional challenges.
Ensure clear governance and escalation paths that empower functional leaders while maintaining institutional cohesion.
Chair the Laboratory's Emergency Policy Committee (EPC) and lead the emergency preparedness, crisis response, and continuity of operations framework.
Serve as the Laboratory’s Responsible Official for the South Coast Air Quality Management District (SCAQMD).
Provide executive oversight of the Ethics, Ombuds, Office of Safety and Mission Success Offices.
Champion executive talent development, succession planning, leadership development, while establishing and maintaining clear performance standards and accountability for Executive Council members and their organizations.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree required.
A minimum of 15 years of executive leadership experience in a highly complex, mission-driven scientific, engineering, aerospace, defense, or national security organization, with demonstrated success developing strategy and driving operational excellence, institutional stewardship, and mission success.
Demonstrated executive leadership across the lifecycle of complex spaceflight programs, including formulation, development, integration, launch, and mission operations.
Experience operating within complex federal acquisition and government contracting environments.
Strong financial and business acumen, including oversight of large budgets, government contracts, and enterprise resource planning.
Demonstrated executive leadership in organizational development, workforce strategy, succession planning, and the recruitment, development, and retention of world-class technical and administrative talent.
Exceptional communication skills and executive presence, with the ability to engage effectively across organizational levels and with senior government officials.
Demonstrated integrity, sound judgment, and leadership that inspires trust and credibility with employees, NASA, Caltech, government agencies, industry partners, and other key stakeholders.
Ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) security clearance within one year of employment.

Preferred Qualifications

Executive leadership experience within NASA, the Department of War, the Intelligence Community, the national security space, or another federal science and technology organization.
Experience leading large-scale spaceflight, aerospace, or scientific programs, with a comprehensive understanding of mission formulation, acquisition strategy, budget development, mission assurance, government partnerships, international collaboration, and regulatory compliance.
Demonstrated success leading organizational transformation.
Demonstrated experience leading diverse, high-performing teams and fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Advanced degree in engineering, science, business administration, public administration, or related discipline.

jobs.description:
"Alpha School students, on average, experience 2.4 to 2.6 times the academic growth of traditional school students"

— Forbes

Alpha is hiring.

The families who choose Alpha rarely arrive from an ad. They arrive because another family sat across from them at dinner and said, "This changed my kid." That word-of-mouth engine is the thing you would own for an entire region: the dinners, the parent ambassadors, the mayor's office, the CEO who opens a door for a 14-year-old's first real project.

A normal week puts you in four rooms. You design and host the region's calendar of gatherings, from a 150-person open house to an eight-seat curated dinner, several a month. You recruit current parents who genuinely want to talk to prospective ones and match them, family to family. You build relationships with city officials and business leaders, turning them into venues, sources of support for new campus openings, and real opportunities for students. And you deliver on the Alpha Networks: introductions, expert masterclasses, internships, alumni welcomes, logged family by family.

There is no finished playbook. You write it while running it, and the systems you invent get picked up by peers building the same engine in other cities. As the region grows, the scoreboard gets harder, not easier: doors opened per family has to rise even as enrollment climbs. Success shows up as the share of growth arriving through real people vouching for Alpha, read on a multi-year trend rather than a quarterly report.

No degree is required, and no particular pedigree. An MBA, a consulting or wealth-management career, and a self-made run in community, hospitality, or advancement all count the same here. What we read is the track record of convening people and turning those relationships into value.

This role is on-site in one of the following regions: Miami, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Boston, Dallas, or New York City. Expect evenings and weekends in rooms full of high-expectation parents, elected officials, and founders, plus regular local travel. You will be the most connected person in your city, and you will spend that on kids. If that trade sounds like the point rather than the cost, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Designing and running the region's gathering calendar: open events, curated dinners by city and grade, and family retreats, several a month and on budget
Securing venues, hosts, and vendors, then hosting the room live
Recruiting current parents as ambassadors, equipping them with true stories, and matching them to prospective families and tours
Opening relationships with public officials and business executives, and turning them into venues, campus-opening support, and student opportunities
Matching enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, masterclasses, and real-world internships, and welcoming graduating families as alumni within 30 days
Logging every gathering, introduction, and first-contact attribution in the CRM (customer relationship management platform) so "doors opened per family" is a true number

What You Won’t Be Doing

Growth here is not bought — no paid media, no ad spend, no impression or lead-volume targets
Owning the brand story or top-down campaigns; Marketing has that
Processing admissions, running tours, or chasing enrollment paperwork; Admissions and Family Success have that
Running a campus day-to-day, or opening the physical building
Reporting raw attendance and headcount as if a full room were the result
Waiting for a finished playbook, a template, or support staff before you start

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Make people-first referrals the majority source of your region's enrollment growth.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building communities or relationship programs in K-12 education, membership, or a comparable network business, where growth came through people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client book, with numbers to show for it
Has personally designed and run 20+ gatherings across the full range, from intimate curated dinners to 100+ person open events, with budget ownership
Has opened and maintained relationships with public officials or business executives that produced concrete, nameable value
Disciplined CRM or relationship-tracking user; logging relationships, first-contact attribution, follow-ups, and actions is already a habit
Lives in, or would return or relocate to, one of these regions where you already have a deep local relationship network: Miami, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Boston, Dallas, or New York City
Available to host on weekday evenings and weekends as a regular rhythm, with local travel
Authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Ran regional growth, community, or partnerships for a network-shaped organization: a school group, membership club, franchise, or faith or civic institution
Built and monetized a high-trust book of relationships as a client-facing principal in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Came up through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and were always the one asked to host and represent the institution
Existing relationships with local government or the business community in your city
Fluent in how families make high-stakes education decisions

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

Employment of residents and housing participants;

Physical modernization of structures and grounds.

Prepare and update tribal data on the Formula Response Form and submit to the IHBG Formula Center annually.

Identify additional funding sources.

Description

Mission:
The Link works with youth and young families to overcome the impacts of poverty and social injustice. Our 23 programs provide supportive housing, intensive case management services, and skills development to youth at risk of or experiencing homelessness, sex trafficking and/or involvement in the juvenile justice system. The Link prides itself on its innovative, youth-centered, strengths-based programming for youth and families as well as programs that are co-designed, implemented and overseen by youth.

Position Specifics

Hiring Salary Range: $96,004.00-$112,005.00/year based on qualifications
Job Type: Full-Time, Exempt
Location: North Minneapolis
Hours/Days: Monday-Friday 9:00-5:00
Note: This position requires driving. To be able to drive on behalf of The Link, candidates must have a valid driver's license, have a safe and reliable vehicle, be able to successfully clear a criminal and motor vehicle background check, and maintain personal insurance at the levels of $100,000 Bodily Injury/Per Person and $300,000 Bodily Injury/Per Accident. Job offer is contingent on having these requirements.

BASIC FUNCTION

The Link seeks a strategic Development Director who is committed to reducing and ending youth homelessness, sex trafficking and reforming the Juvenile Justice System to join its executive team. This integral position will contribute to the advancement of the organization’s mission work with youth and young families. The Development Director is responsible for planning and implementing a comprehensive development strategy that encompasses communications, marketing and all private fundraising for the organization including individual and major gifts, foundation giving, corporate partnerships, planned giving, annual appeals, and fundraising events. This position will heavily concentrate on increasing annual fund revenue through segmented solicitation, prospecting, acquisition and retention efforts.

Annual Fund (70%)

Develop and implement a comprehensive development strategy and annual plan to meet the organization’s development goals
Work closely with the Executive Team to establish a fundraising plan and participate in developing the overall strategic plan for the organization
Research new donor prospects and gift opportunities; make recommendations to the Development team and leadership on which to pursue
Researches, identifies, and contacts potential funding sources whose guidelines and requirements match those of the agency
Develops and implements strategies for securing major gifts in collaboration with the CEO and COO
Creates and implements donor segmentation for portfolio management and segmented solicitations

Job Details

New ideas are all around us, but only a few will change the world. That’s our focus at JPL. We ask the biggest questions, then search the universe for answers—literally. We build upon ideas that have guided generations, then share our discoveries to inspire generations to come. Your mission—your opportunity—is to seek out the answers that bring us one step closer. If you’re driven to discover, create, and inspire something that lasts a lifetime and beyond, you’re ready for JPL.

Located in Pasadena, California, JPL has a campus-like environment situated on 177 acres in the foothills of the San Gabriel Mountains and offers a work environment unlike any other: we inspire passion, foster innovation, build collaboration, and reward excellence.

Summary

The Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), a federally funded research and development center managed by the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) for NASA, is seeking an exceptional executive leader to serve as its Deputy Director/Chief Operating Officer and help shape the future of one of the world's premier aerospace and research institutions, enabling groundbreaking discoveries, advancing national priorities, and supporting missions that expand humanity's understanding of Earth, the solar system, and the universe. Partnering closely with the Director, the Deputy Director will provide strategic leadership, institutional stewardship, and operational excellence across a complex enterprise of scientific, engineering, and administrative functions. The successful candidate will empower a world-class workforce while strengthening the partnerships, capabilities, and organizational resilience necessary to achieve JPL's ambitious mission now and into the future.

Job Summary

The Deputy Director of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory is appointed by the Vice President/ Director of JPL with the concurrence of the President of the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), which manages JPL for NASA, and in consultation with the NASA Administrator.

Reporting to the JPL Director, the Deputy Director serves as the Laboratory's Chief Operating Officer, providing executive leadership for institutional operations and mission execution. The Deputy Director leads and integrates the Executive Council, drives organizational execution and accountability, and provides strategic leadership for the Laboratory's workforce. As a strategic partner to the Director, the Deputy Director orchestrates cross-functional coordination among Business, Operations, and Programmatic leadership while maintaining institutional alignment and operational continuity. The Deputy Director ensures operational excellence, fosters a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement, and engages in strategic relationships with NASA, Caltech, the Department of War, Intelligence Community, and Space Force. Through integrated execution across programmatic and institutional functions, the Deputy Director ensures operational excellence across all Laboratory functions, driving continuous improvement while deepening the critical Caltech-JPL partnership.

Key Responsibilities

Executive Leadership

Provide executive leadership and ensure integration of the Laboratory's institutional operations, which includes acquisitions, workforce management, infrastructure, facilities, and administrative organizations.
Partner with the JPL Director to establish institutional priorities, execute strategic initiatives, and advance the Laboratory's long-term vision.
Continue to strengthen and advance the close and enduring partnership with Caltech
Serve as Acting Director, when delegated, exercising full authority for Laboratory operations and executive decision-making.
Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, integrity, and continuous improvement.
Support and partner with the Director in leading the Laboratory through periods of organizational change while maintaining workforce engagement, operational continuity, and mission success.
Chair the weekly Executive Council, facilitating Laboratory-wide decision-making, policy development, and organizational alignment.

Strategic Institutional Leadership

Assume a leadership role in the development and execution of JPL's long-range institutional strategy, which includes aligning workforce, infrastructure, technology investments, and operational capabilities with future mission needs. Ensure Executive Council alignment on institutional strategy and drive integrated execution across programmatic and institutional functions.
Initiate organizational assessments and continuous improvement initiatives to enhance institutional effectiveness.
Oversee Laboratory-level governance, management systems, and enterprise decision making processes to ensure transparency, accountability, compliance, and organizational performance.
Deepen the enduring partnership with Caltech administration, participating in Caltech Board of Trustees engagements concerning JPL.

Programmatic Oversight

Chair Center Project Management Reviews (PMR) to evaluate mission readiness, risk posture, and programmatic execution across all spaceflight and scientific projects.
Serve as JPL's senior representative to the NASA Office of JPL Management and Oversight (NOJMO), while acting as the primary institutional liaison with NASA and Caltech functional leadership.
Ensure effective integration of mission, compliance, and institutional functions across the organization.
With the Director, lead JPL's strategic relationships with the Department of War, the Intelligence Community, and the U.S. Space Force, serving as the primary executive interface for national security programs.

Institutional Processes and Operations

Facilitate cross-functional coordination among Business, Operations, and Programmatic leadership to drive aligned execution and resolve cross-functional institutional challenges.
Ensure clear governance and escalation paths that empower functional leaders while maintaining institutional cohesion.
Chair the Laboratory's Emergency Policy Committee (EPC) and lead the emergency preparedness, crisis response, and continuity of operations framework.
Serve as the Laboratory’s Responsible Official for the South Coast Air Quality Management District (SCAQMD).
Provide executive oversight of the Ethics, Ombuds, Office of Safety and Mission Success Offices.
Champion executive talent development, succession planning, leadership development, while establishing and maintaining clear performance standards and accountability for Executive Council members and their organizations.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree required.
A minimum of 15 years of executive leadership experience in a highly complex, mission-driven scientific, engineering, aerospace, defense, or national security organization, with demonstrated success developing strategy and driving operational excellence, institutional stewardship, and mission success.
Demonstrated executive leadership across the lifecycle of complex spaceflight programs, including formulation, development, integration, launch, and mission operations.
Experience operating within complex federal acquisition and government contracting environments.
Strong financial and business acumen, including oversight of large budgets, government contracts, and enterprise resource planning.
Demonstrated executive leadership in organizational development, workforce strategy, succession planning, and the recruitment, development, and retention of world-class technical and administrative talent.
Exceptional communication skills and executive presence, with the ability to engage effectively across organizational levels and with senior government officials.
Demonstrated integrity, sound judgment, and leadership that inspires trust and credibility with employees, NASA, Caltech, government agencies, industry partners, and other key stakeholders.
Ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) security clearance within one year of employment.

Preferred Qualifications

Executive leadership experience within NASA, the Department of War, the Intelligence Community, the national security space, or another federal science and technology organization.
Experience leading large-scale spaceflight, aerospace, or scientific programs, with a comprehensive understanding of mission formulation, acquisition strategy, budget development, mission assurance, government partnerships, international collaboration, and regulatory compliance.
Demonstrated success leading organizational transformation.
Demonstrated experience leading diverse, high-performing teams and fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Advanced degree in engineering, science, business administration, public administration, or related discipline.

"Alpha School students, on average, experience 2.4 to 2.6 times the academic growth of traditional school students"

— Forbes

Alpha is hiring.

The families who choose Alpha rarely arrive from an ad. They arrive because another family sat across from them at dinner and said, "This changed my kid." That word-of-mouth engine is the thing you would own for an entire region: the dinners, the parent ambassadors, the mayor's office, the CEO who opens a door for a 14-year-old's first real project.

A normal week puts you in four rooms. You design and host the region's calendar of gatherings, from a 150-person open house to an eight-seat curated dinner, several a month. You recruit current parents who genuinely want to talk to prospective ones and match them, family to family. You build relationships with city officials and business leaders, turning them into venues, sources of support for new campus openings, and real opportunities for students. And you deliver on the Alpha Networks: introductions, expert masterclasses, internships, alumni welcomes, logged family by family.

There is no finished playbook. You write it while running it, and the systems you invent get picked up by peers building the same engine in other cities. As the region grows, the scoreboard gets harder, not easier: doors opened per family has to rise even as enrollment climbs. Austin, TX (In Office, Full Time)

To grow revenue at selfpublishing.com through high quality, mutually beneficial partnerships and speaking engagements.

Learn our process for finding, reaching out to, and closing partnership deals
Add 200 prospects to your pipeline
Book and run 10 discovery calls

Complete 40 discovery calls
Deliver two speaking events and drive at least $50,000 in revenue

Complete 10+ live events for $500,000+ in stage revenue
Complete 24 affiliate partnerships for $500,000+ in non stage revenue

A natural relationship builder who creates win for win partnerships.

An engaging speaker who is comfortable on stage in front of large audiences.
Organized, proactive, and driven by data.
Someone who enjoys traveling and meeting new people.
A believer in the power of books and personal transformation.

Honesty & Integrity Always Win
Fail Fast, Fail Forward, Fail Often
Hard Work & Continuous Improvement
Everyone Is Responsible For Facilitating Change
Best Is The Standard

Willingness to travel for live events
Ready to work 45+ hours a week

An existing network of affiliate partners, event hosts, or influencers

A published book (or the dream to write one)

You're looking to coast

Top tier healthcare: Your choice of high quality plans for full time employees

Purpose-Driven Work – Make a meaningful impact in the lives of individuals, families, and communities throughout Western Massachusetts.
Professional Growth – Access ongoing training, mentorship, career development, and advancement opportunities across one of the region's largest behavioral health organizations.
Supportive Team Culture – Join a collaborative workplace guided by our HEART values: Humanity, Empowerment, Accountability, Respect, and Teamwork.
Stability & Opportunity – Build your career with a well-established organization serving Western Massachusetts since 1938.
Comprehensive Benefits – Generous PTO, 403(b), educational assistance, medical, dental, vision, employee assistance programs, and more.
Certified Great Place to Work – Work for an organization recognized for creating a positive and engaging employee experience.

What You’ll Do

The Program Director is responsible for managing the FRC’s contractual relationships. The Program Director also manages all communications with EOHHS and DCF and ensures adherence to the contractual obligations. The Program Director works directly with Family Members to carry out center activities. The Program Director may assume some of the functions of the Assistant Program Director.

Manage FRC Contractual Relationships.
Manages relationship with the Administrative Services Organization (ASO) and ensures program adherence to all ASO guidelines and requirements.
Develops and maintains partnerships with community organizations and agencies by creating and maintaining MOUs.
Reviews and analyzes reports to meet program benchmarks.
Plans and participates with families in various FRC activities.
Assumes some of the functions of the Assistant Program Director as needed.
Conducts community outreach throughout catchment area to foster community partnerships and increase awareness of the Family Resource Center.

Who You Are

BA Degree in Human Services or related field
5 years of experience in staff supervision and program management
Familiarity with DCF and other state agencies.
Knowledge of managing contractual relationships with funders and managing a program
Demonstrated willingness and ability to work with client populations from diverse cultural and socioeconomic backgrounds.
Demonstrated ability to provide community-based service.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

Since 1938, BHN has delivered high-quality, culturally responsive behavioral health care, building deep roots in Western Massachusetts while expanding our impact in communities throughout the state. Our core values—Humanity, Empowerment, Accountability, Respect, and Teamwork—guide how we lead, serve, and support one another. If you’re ready to bring your skills and experience to a mission-driven organization where your work can make a meaningful difference, we’d love to hear from you.
